A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Fast-dLLM. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across additions, relocation, and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original accuracy and throughput experiments on LLaDA and Dream, component and parameter ablations, and generated-response case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds multimodal evaluations, factor-decoding experiments, LLaDA-1.5 comparisons, and decoding-efficiency analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 and Algorithm 1 add factor-based decoding: sort token confidences and select the largest n satisfying (n+1)(1-c_(n)) < f, instead of using only a fixed confidence threshold. Section C.1 also introduces an LLaDA-V adaptation that retains a full block and refreshes its cache every r decoding steps. These change token selection and cache-update procedures.

E1.justification: v2 extends the retained GSM8K, MATH, HumanEval, and MBPP coverage to vision-language mathematical reasoning on MathVista and MathVerse using LLaDA-V. Appendix B.4 additionally evaluates image-description generation, introducing visual inputs and task requirements absent from v1.

E2.justification: v2 adds LLaDA-1.5 to a direct comparison with Fast-dLLM on original LLaDA (Table 12), and uses the original threshold strategy as the explicit comparator for factor decoding (Table 11). The original benchmark comparator columns remain. LLaMA already appeared in v1 Figure 1; it is not a newly introduced baseline.

E3.justification: The original benchmark settings remain, but v2 adds substantial experimental protocols. These include MathVista block-length tests at 48 decoding steps, refresh-interval sweeps, factor-value sweeps, and evaluations using LLaDA-1.5. Appendix C.5 introduces a caching-only throughput comparison with 256-token prefills, generation lengths of 16/32/64, and batch sizes from 1 to 32.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's cache, threshold, length, and arithmetic-case analyses, v2 tests why small blocks fail for LLaDA-V and how refresh frequency affects the trade-off. It also compares factor and threshold decoding, analyzes parallel token counts over decoding steps, examines batch-size scaling, and adds a visual-description case study (Appendices B.4 and C).

E5.justification: Figure 7 and Section C.4 newly report a 95% confidence band for average parallel token counts, described as cross-sample variability. v1 has no corresponding uncertainty reporting. This does not establish additional repeated runs; benchmark seed counts and repeated-run uncertainty remain unspecified.

E6.justification: The original benchmark and length-ablation tables retain their numerical values. v2 adds substantial results, including 9.9x and 8.5x multimodal speedups in Table 3. Table 11 reports factor decoding at 78.5 tokens/s and 77.5% accuracy versus threshold decoding at 54.4 tokens/s and 78.5% accuracy on GSM8K with length 256. Additional entries cover LLaDA-1.5, refresh sensitivity, token-count dynamics, and batch scaling; these are new comparisons rather than improvements to unchanged settings.

T1.justification: Theorem 1, its assumptions, tightness construction, distance and KL bounds, and the complete Appendix A proof are unchanged. The new factor-selection procedure draws on the existing bound without adding or revising a theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same scientific claims: approximate KV caching, confidence-aware parallel decoding, and up to 27.6x acceleration with minimal accuracy loss. The added experiments and variants do not revise these headline claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds important applicability qualifications: small-block decoding does not transfer directly to LLaDA-V, and PrefixCache falls behind LLaMA at larger batch sizes, attributed to diffusion models' computational overhead. It also interprets factor decoding as a latency-versus-accuracy trade-off and explains changing parallelism and variability across decoding stages. These substantially extend v1's interpretation of practical deployment.

D1.justification: The new appendix documents reproducibility details for the added experiments, including 96-token multimodal blocks, refresh intervals of 2/4/8/16/32, and the precise prefill, output-length, and batch-size settings for throughput tests. The existing A100 80GB hardware disclosure, lm-eval usage, and code/project links remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to LLaDA-V and LLaDA 1.5 to support the expanded evaluations. The related-work discussion and positioning against earlier diffusion and acceleration approaches are otherwise retained; shifted reference numbers do not represent additional changes.

P1.justification: Most existing prose remains unchanged, including the abstract, introduction, conclusion, related work, and proof. Local additions explain factor decoding and the new results, while Appendix B.4 and Appendix C extend the document structure. This is an extension rather than extensive rewriting or reorganization.

P2.justification: v2 adds multimodal, refresh-sensitivity, strategy-comparison, and model-comparison tables (Tables 3 and 9-12). Figures 6-9 introduce an illustrated response comparison, a confidence-band plot, factor-decoding panels, and batch-scaling curves. Figure 4 is resized and repositioned, while retained tables are renumbered. These substantially expand the visual presentation of the evidence.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens assessment of applicability and deployment trade-offs beyond v1's predominantly single-batch, text-only evidence. It exposes multimodal small-block failures and large-batch disadvantages against autoregressive decoding, tests a cache-refresh adaptation, and evaluates the factor strategy's accuracy-throughput trade-off. These address important gaps behind the practical-deployment claims. Some added interpretation is overstated: Section C.3 claims consistent LLaDA-1.5 benefits although Table 12 shows worse MATH accuracy and throughput at length 512. That reporting weakness tempers, but does not outweigh, the substantive gains.
